## Working papers

### An Industry-Level Measure of Quality-Adjusted Human Capital in the European Union

*With [Juan Durán Vanegas](#) and [Iulia Siedschlag](#). ESRI Working Paper No. 812, October 2025.* \
[[Paper]](files/Duran-Jordan-Siedschlag_2025_QAHC-EU_paper.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-secondary}
[[Policy brief]](files/Duran-Jordan-Siedschlag_2025_QAHC-EU_brief.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-secondary}

We construct a novel quality-adjusted human capital (QAHC) measure at the industry level for the European Union and the UK over 2010–2021. The measure combines education quality — from PISA (together with historical test-score series) and PIAAC — with education quantity (mean years of schooling), and maps these to industry-level employment composition using EU KLEMS and INTANProd. In a Stochastic Frontier model the measure yields reasonable output elasticities and is statistically linked to labour-productivity growth, particularly in goods-producing industries, unlike traditional education-attainment proxies.

### The Impact of Light Rail Transit Extensions on Residential Property Prices: Evidence from Dublin's Luas Cross City Project

*Undergraduate thesis, Trinity College Dublin, April 2024. Supervisor: Ronan Lyons.* \
[[Thesis]](files/Jordan_2024_Luas-LRT_thesis.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-secondary}

I estimate the capitalisation of the 2017 Luas Cross City extension into residential property prices in North Inner City Dublin. Starting from a Dublin sales dataset of 44,894 transactions scraped from Daft.ie — cleaned, de-duplicated, geocoded via the Google Geocoding API, and assigned to small-area geographies — I engineer treatment exposure using Euclidean distance to new Luas stops and implement hedonic, difference-in-differences, and instrumental variables designs. Post-opening, I estimate a 5.78% price premium within 1,000m (DiD) and 13.1% at 400–800m (IV), consistent with a non-linear distance gradient.
